name: coding-agent identifiers
description: Identifier-heavy recall for the coding-agent wedge (ROADMAP 4.1). Every query is the kind a developer actually types mid-task — a flag, an env var, a file:line, an error string, a symbol — and every relevant memory is the one that literally contains that token. Run it with `make eval EVAL_ARGS='--lexical --dataset eval/datasets/identifiers.json'` to compare all three retrieval modes. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the default `hashing` embedder is itself token-based (it hashes whitespace/alnum tokens into buckets), so it behaves like a lexical matcher and scores far better on these queries than a real dense embedding model would — it is NOT a stand-in for the weakness this dataset is meant to expose. With the default embedder this set works as a regression gate (hybrid must not lose to semantic-only, and must not drop a query semantic-only answered); to see the actual size of the gap, run it against a real model via --embedder command --embedder-cmd.

memories.label: tenant_max_records
memories.text: Per-tenant storage is capped with --tenant-max-records and --tenant-max-bytes. A tenant past either cap gets QUOTA_EXCEEDED on insert; deletes still work so it can recover on its own.

memories.label: tenant_rate_qps
memories.text: Request rate is bounded per namespace by --tenant-rate-qps with a --tenant-rate-burst allowance. Over the rate the server answers RATE_LIMITED rather than queueing.

memories.label: recall_top_k_env
memories.text: The Claude Code recall hook is capped by the AEGIS_RECALL_TOP_K environment variable, set in settings.json. The hook does not inherit the .mcp.json env, so it falls back to embedding_mode none.

memories.label: hnsw_crc_fix
memories.text: The CRC framing bug that dropped records after a torn write was fixed in hnsw.c:214 — the length prefix was read before the magic was validated.

memories.label: query_scan_cap
memories.text: A filterless search is bounded by --query-scan-cap (default 100000) so one broad query cannot pull the whole dataset into RAM. When the cap truncates, count reports a floor rather than an exact number.

memories.label: max_index_bytes
memories.text: Index RAM backpressure is configured with --max-index-bytes. Past the cap inserts return MEMORY_LIMIT while deletes and updates still proceed, so the operator can free space.

memories.label: no_lexical_index
memories.text: Passing --no-lexical-index skips the BM25 keyword index and saves its RAM, but a search carrying a query string then returns NOT_READY.

memories.label: header_rebuild
memories.text: The Makefile tracks header dependencies with -MMD -MP, so editing a header in include/ rebuilds every object that included it. The old advice to run make clean first no longer applies.

memories.label: auth_token_file
memories.text: Tokens are loaded from --auth-token-file, one 'secret namespace scope' triple per line; a bare line is a global admin token. Runtime token_add rewrites the file with every entry hashed.

memories.label: embedding_dim_mismatch
memories.text: A search whose embedding length differs from --embedding-dim is rejected with INVALID_REQUEST. Restoring a snapshot into a server with a different dimension is refused for the same reason.

memories.label: fsync_batch
memories.text: Durability mode is chosen with --fsync-batch or --fsync-interval-ms; with neither, every append fsyncs. The stats response reports whichever tuning value is active.

memories.label: log_generation
memories.text: Compaction bumps log_generation, and a replica watching the stream re-bootstraps because its byte-offset cursor into the old log is no longer valid.

memories.label: make_eval_decay
memories.text: Forgetting is measured with make eval EVAL_ARGS='--decay': it seeds low-value episodic noise and asserts the corpus plateaus while recall@10 holds.

memories.label: supersedes_link
memories.text: Consolidation records a supersedes relationship from the surviving record to each absorbed one, so a merge is auditable lineage instead of silent loss.

memories.label: blue_green_rejected
memories.text: The blue-green migration approach was rejected last quarter: it doubled the infrastructure bill for a service whose deploys are already sub-minute. Canary rollout was chosen instead.

memories.label: working_capacity
memories.text: Volatile working memory is a per-session ring buffer sized by --working-capacity, with entries expiring after --default-ttl-ms unless promoted.

queries.text: why does the build need a clean rebuild after a header edit?
which migration approach did we reject and why?
how do I stop one tenant filling the disk?
